simple.meaning: תְּמוּרָה (tᵉmûwrâh) is a Hebrew word meaning “barter , compensation.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: תְּמוּרָה (H8545) appears 6 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Leviticus 27:10, with occurrences in Leviticus, Ruth, Job.

definitions.full: H8545. temurah תְּמוּרָה noun feminine exchange, recompense ; — ׳ת Ruth 4:7 ; suffix תְּמוּרָתוֺ Lev 27:10 3 t.; תְּמוּרָתָהּ Job 28:17 ; — exchange = thing acquired by exchange Lev 27:10 , 33 ; Job 28:17 ; תְּמוּרָתוֺ חֵיל 20:18 wealth acquired by exchange (figurative; read possibly הֵילוֺ as his wealth (so) his exchange , Bu); recompense (for worldliness) 15:31 ; abstract exchanging Ruth 4:7 (|| גְּאוּלָּה ). מֹר מוֺר, see מרר . מוֺרָא , I. מוֺרָה see יָרֵא .

occurrences.englishText: He shall not alter it, nor exchange it, a good for a bad, or a bad for a good. If he shall at all exchange animal for animal, then both it and that for which it is exchanged shall be holy.
He shall not examine whether it is good or bad, neither shall he exchange it. If he exchanges it at all, then both it and that for which it is exchanged shall be holy. It shall not be redeemed.’ ”

Now this was the custom in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning exchanging, to confirm all things: a man took off his sandal, and gave it to his neighbor; and this was the way of formalizing transactions in Israel.
Let him not trust in emptiness, deceiving himself;
He will restore that for which he labored, and will not swallow it down.
